takeaway: Hepatitis B is the second most common human carcinogen worldwide after tobacco; it is prevented by vaccination.

question.say: With regard to hepatitis B, which statement is true?

answer.text: It is the second most common human carcinogen worldwide
answer.say: The answer: it is the second most common human carcinogen worldwide.

lines.text: The hepatitis B virus wins the silver medal.
lines.say: (laugh) The hepatitis B virus proudly wears the silver medal.

lines.text: Tobacco stands first on the podium.
lines.say: Tobacco stands on the top step, as the most common human carcinogen.

lines.text: Hepatitis B is the second most common carcinogen worldwide.
lines.say: After tobacco smoking, hepatitis B is the second most common human carcinogen worldwide.

lines.text: It is prevented by vaccination, not treated.
lines.say: Hepatitis B is effectively prevented, not treated, by hepatitis B vaccination.

lines.text: Vaccination is mandatory for healthcare professionals who meet blood products.
lines.say: Vaccination is mandatory for all healthcare professionals who regularly come into contact with blood products.

lines.text: Remember: hepatitis B is second only to tobacco as a carcinogen.
lines.say: Remember: hepatitis B is second only to tobacco as a human carcinogen.
